html:
The Magyars, or Hungarians, are a people who speak a Uralic language, related to Finnish and Estonian rather than to their neighbours. On the map for 700 to 900 they are on the steppe north of the Black Sea, and by 1000 they hold the Carpathian Basin.

On the steppe they lived as horse herders, for a time allied with the Khazars. Around 895, under attack from the Pechenegs and led by Árpád, they crossed the Carpathians and settled the plain of Hungary, ending what was left of Great Moravia.

For half a century their mounted raiders struck deep into Germany, Italy and France. The raids stopped after the German king Otto I beat them at the Lechfeld in 955. The Magyars then settled down to farming. Their ruler Stephen I was crowned a Christian king in 1000, and the tribes became the kingdom of Hungary.
